name: Bone Density Hypermineralization
description: Dramatically increases bone mineral density by introducing genes from the African elephant and the whale, species whose bones are among the densest in the animal kingdom. The user's skeleton becomes extraordinarily resistant to fracture — falls, impacts, and blunt trauma that would shatter normal bones produce bruises at worst. The modification adds 5–10 kg of body mass from the denser bone alone. Combined with osteodermal plating, the result is a human body that approaches light-vehicle crash resistance. The trade-off is weight, reduced buoyancy (stone-boned individuals sink like rocks in water), and the fact that denser bones transmit impact force more efficiently to joints and soft tissue — the bones won't break, but the joints and organs behind them still take the hit. Crucible Genomics' installation includes joint reinforcement to partially address this limitation.
source_organism: Loxodonta africana (African elephant), Balaenoptera musculus (blue whale, hypermineralized bone genes)
procedure: Systemic retroviral injection targeting osteoblast activity, 4 sessions over 2 months
reversibility: Partially reversible with osteoclast stimulation; bone density decreases but never returns to baseline
side_effects: 5–10 kg weight gain from bone mass alone
Cannot float — swimming becomes life-threatening without assistance
Joint stress from increased bone mass
Metal detectors occasionally trigger from mineral density
Medical imaging becomes difficult — X-rays have trouble penetrating hypermineralized bone
social_perception: Practical and unglamorous. Stone Bones is a working-class modification for people who get hit for a living — fighters, construction workers, anyone in high-impact environments. The weight penalty limits its appeal for aesthetics-focused users.
story_hooks: A Stone Bones user falls from a great height and survives — the bones hold, but the internal organ damage reveals the modification's limitation: the bones transmit all the force to everything behind them
A hypermineralized skeleton is found in the harbor — the body sank immediately when dumped, making it the perfect way to dispose of someone with this specific modification
